newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria steps up fight against white collar crime.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria steps up fight against white collar crime.

text.p: Bulgarian police have uncovered widespread economic crimes accounting for some 30.6 billion levs ($19 million) since the start of the year, the interior ministry said on Tuesday.

The interim government which took office in February vowed to crack down on white collar crime, and Interior Minister Bogomil Bonev will retain his post in the new cabinet to be declared on Wednesday.

"We have set new priorities for the economic police in line with the ongoing structural reforms and we have already made progress in fighting smuggling, fraud, and embezzlement," said Mincho Yashev, head of the ministry's economic police department.
He told a news conference police had seized more than 200,000 pirate audio compact discs in the first four months of the year.
"We are determined to change Bulgaria's reputation as the second biggest producer of pirate CDs after China," he said.
Yashev said the interim cabinet had succeeded in reducing smuggling by placing police officers alongside customs officers at border checkpoints.

"We have stopped the illegal export and smuggling of goods worth more than 14 billion levs, but besides this the presence of police officers has a psychological effect on the customs officers and they are motivated to do their job better," he said.

Yashev said the economic police would monitor all voucher funds set up under Bulgaria's mass privatisation programme. The funds bring together the vouchers issued to individuals, which can be exchanged for shares, and invest them.

"Control of the privatisation funds will not be easy because even the Czech Republic had problems with white collar crime while implementing its privatisation programme but we have experienced the effect of financial pyramids and we will take all necessary steps in this aspect," Yashev said.

Bulgaria's legal system has struggled to keep pace with changes since the end of one-party communist rule. Crime and corruption have flourished and large sums of money have been siphoned out of the country.
